standard_prerequisites.name: The presheaf Z_X represented by an object X of the category
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Notation of this chapter: for an object X the presheaf Z_X assigns to Y the free abelian group on Hom(Y, X); the chain complex Z_{U, bullet} is built from these
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the meaning of the summands of the displayed chain complex and of the alternating sign maps between them; the identification of maps out of the complex is the counted content.

standard_prerequisites.name: Hom out of a direct sum of representable presheaves into a presheaf
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Modules on Sites, Lemma labelled sites-modules-lemma-obvious-adjointness (canonical Stacks tag 03A8); invoked at proof line 1021
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the two displayed equalities Hom(sum, F) = prod Hom(representable, F) = prod F(...); the resulting term-by-term identification with the Cech complex is inside the counted span.

core_obligations: Compute maps out of the chain complex term by term: for each p use that a map out of the direct sum of the presheaves Z_{U_{i_0} x_U ... x_U U_{i_p}} is the product of the individual Hom groups, and that a map out of a representable presheaf Z_X into F is just an element of F(X), as displayed in the two equalities of the proof (proof lines 1006-1020).

Identify the result with the Cech complex: the product of the values F(U_{i_0} x_U ... x_U U_{i_p}) over all index tuples with repetitions is exactly the degree p term of the Cech complex of the family U with coefficients in F, and the alternating sign convention of the differentials matches, so the two complexes are termwise equal (proof lines 1006-1021).

Record functoriality: the identification is natural in the abelian presheaf F because both sides are built from the values F(U_{i_0} x_U ... x_U U_{i_p}) by the same product and the same sign rule, which is the functoriality asserted in the statement (statement line 1002, proof line 1021).
proof_roadmap: Expand a map of complexes out of Z_{U, bullet} into F in each degree using the sum/product adjunction for presheaves (proof lines 1006-1020).
Recognise the resulting product of values of F on fibre products as the Cech complex, matching degrees and the alternating signs of the differentials (proof lines 1006-1021).
Note that the identification is functorial in F, which completes the statement (proof line 1021).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the complex of maps from the Cech chain complex Z_{U, bullet} of a family U = {U_i -> U} into an abelian presheaf F with the Cech complex of U with coefficients in F, functorially in F (statement lines 972-1002). The proof is short but not a hypothesis-checking step: it expands a map out of a direct sum of representable presheaves into F into a product of values F(U_{i_0} x_U ... x_U U_{i_p}), displayed as two equalities, and then has to match the alternating sign convention of the differentials of Z_{U, bullet} with the sign convention of the Cech differential (proof lines 1006-1021). What makes the statement usable later is exactly the functoriality in F asserted in its last clause. The claim is H2: one adjunction computation whose content is the degree and sign bookkeeping.
